title: Ice Age cold snap ends
description: The Younger Dryas cold spell ends around 9700 BCE and the warmer Holocene begins, helping the first farmers.

title: Göbekli Tepe built
description: People build circles of carved stone pillars at Göbekli Tepe, among the world’s oldest known megaliths.

title: Jericho settled
description: The first settlement at Jericho, one of the oldest towns in the world, later protected by a stone wall and tower.

title: Farming begins
description: In the Fertile Crescent people domesticate wheat, barley, sheep and goats: the start of the Neolithic Revolution.
source: Wikipedia: Neolithic Revolution (date from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Rice domesticated in China
description: Asian rice is domesticated in China, some 13,500 to 8,200 years ago; it later feeds half the world.

title: Çatalhöyük at its height
description: A very large Neolithic town in Anatolia, with houses entered through the roof, flourishes around 7000 BCE.

title: Maize domesticated in Mexico
description: Indigenous peoples in southern Mexico breed maize from the wild grass teosinte.
source: Wikipedia: Maize (date from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Doggerland lost to the sea
description: Rising seas drown Doggerland, the land bridge between Britain and Europe.
source: Wikipedia: Doggerland (date from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: The 8.2-kiloyear cold event
description: A sudden drop in global temperatures around 8,200 years ago lasts two to four centuries.

title: Oldest gold treasure (Varna)
description: Graves at Varna in Bulgaria hold the oldest known gold jewellery in the world (4600–4200 BCE).

title: Carnac standing stones
description: More than 3,000 standing stones are raised in rows in Brittany.
source: Wikipedia: Carnac stones (date from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Uruk: the first cities
description: Uruk grows into one of the first true cities, leading to writing by the end of the 4th millennium BCE.

title: The wheel
description: Early wheeled vehicles appear in Mesopotamia and nearby regions, about 3500 BCE.
source: Wikipedia: Wheel (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Horses at Botai
description: The Botai culture of Kazakhstan (c. 3700–3100 BCE) relies heavily on horses; whether they were domesticated is debated.

title: Ötzi the Iceman
description: A Copper Age man dies in the Alps; his natural mummy, found in 1991, is Europe’s oldest.

title: Cuneiform writing appears
description: In Uruk, Sumerian scribes develop cuneiform, one of the earliest known writing systems, first used for accounts and records.

title: Unification of Egypt
description: Upper and Lower Egypt are united under one king, traditionally Narmer (Menes), beginning about 3,000 years of pharaonic rule.

title: Caral’s great pyramids
description: Caral–Supe builders raise platform mounds and sunken plazas, the oldest monumental city in the Americas.
source: Wikipedia: Caral (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Great Pyramid of Giza
description: The pyramid of Khufu is completed, the tallest human-made structure in the world for nearly 4,000 years.

title: Mohenjo-daro at its height
description: The Indus city of Mohenjo-daro flourishes, with a grid plan, brick houses and advanced drainage.

title: Stonehenge
description: The great sarsen stones of Stonehenge are raised in southern Britain (around 2500 BCE).
source: Wikipedia: Stonehenge (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Sargon founds the Akkadian Empire
description: Sargon of Akkad unites the Sumerian city-states, creating what is often called the first empire.

title: Enheduanna, first named author
description: Sargon’s daughter, high priestess at Ur, writes hymns: the earliest known author known by name.
source: Wikipedia: Enheduanna (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: The 4.2-kiloyear drought
description: A severe, long drought affects many regions and is linked to the fall of the Akkadian Empire.

title: Palace of Knossos
description: The Minoan palace complex at Knossos on Crete becomes a major centre of trade and art.

title: Decline of the Indus cities
description: The great Indus cities are gradually abandoned. Climate change and shifting rivers are leading explanations, but the causes are debated.

title: Code of Hammurabi
description: King Hammurabi of Babylon issues one of the earliest surviving written law codes, carved on a stone stele.

title: Thera (Santorini) eruption
description: A massive volcanic eruption buries the town of Akrotiri. Its effect on the Minoans is debated.

title: Hittites sack Babylon
description: The Hittite king Mursili I raids and sacks Babylon, ending the First Babylonian dynasty.

title: Akhenaten’s religious revolution
description: Pharaoh Akhenaten promotes the worship of the sun-disk Aten and builds a new capital at Amarna.

title: Battle of Kadesh
description: Egypt under Ramesses II and the Hittites under Muwatalli II fight one of the largest chariot battles known.

title: Egyptian–Hittite peace treaty
description: Ramesses II and Hattusili III sign one of the earliest known peace treaties.

title: Oldest Chinese inscriptions
description: Oracle-bone inscriptions from the Shang capital near Anyang are the earliest surviving Chinese writing.

title: Olmec colossal heads
description: The Olmec of San Lorenzo carve giant basalt heads, probably portraits of rulers.

title: Late Bronze Age collapse
description: Many eastern Mediterranean states, including the Hittites and Mycenaean Greece, collapse within a few decades amid drought, migration and war.

title: Phoenician alphabet
description: The Phoenician alphabet, ancestor of the Greek, Latin and Arabic scripts, is in use.

title: Zhou conquer the Shang
description: The Zhou defeat the Shang at the Battle of Muye and justify it with the Mandate of Heaven.

title: Carthage founded
description: Settlers from Tyre found Carthage in North Africa (traditional date 814 BCE).

title: First recorded Olympic Games
description: The traditional date for the first Olympic Games at Olympia.

title: Legendary founding of Rome
description: The traditional date for Romulus founding Rome. Archaeology shows earlier settlement.

title: Kushite kings rule Egypt
description: Kings of Kush from Napata conquer Egypt and rule as its Twenty-fifth Dynasty.
source: Wikipedia: Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Assyria conquers the Kingdom of Israel
description: The Neo-Assyrian Empire captures Samaria and deports much of the population of the northern Kingdom of Israel.
source: Wikipedia: Assyrian captivity of Israel (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Library of Ashurbanipal
description: The Assyrian king gathers tens of thousands of clay tablets at Nineveh, including the Epic of Gilgamesh.

title: First coins
description: The kingdom of Lydia in Anatolia issues some of the earliest known coins, made of electrum.

title: Fall of Nineveh
description: Babylonians, Medes and Scythians sack the Assyrian capital, Nineveh.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of Nineveh (612 BC) (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Babylon destroys Jerusalem
description: Nebuchadnezzar II destroys Jerusalem and its temple and deports Judeans to Babylon.
source: Wikipedia: Siege of Jerusalem (587 BC) (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Ishtar Gate
description: Nebuchadnezzar II builds the blue-glazed Ishtar Gate of Babylon (c. 569 BCE).

title: Confucius
description: The philosopher Confucius teaches in the state of Lu. His ideas about ethics, family and government become central to Chinese civilisation.

title: Cyrus the Great takes Babylon
description: Cyrus conquers Babylon and allows exiled peoples, including the Judeans, to return home.

title: Roman Republic founded
description: Rome expels its last king and establishes a republic governed by elected magistrates and the Senate.

title: Athenian democracy
description: Cleisthenes’ reforms create a democracy for Athens’ male citizens.

title: Battle of Marathon
description: Athens defeats a Persian invasion force, a key moment in the Greco-Persian Wars.

title: The Buddha
description: Siddhartha Gautama teaches in northern India; the dates of his life (5th century BCE) are debated.

title: Thermopylae and Salamis
description: Greek city-states resist Xerxes I’s invasion; the Persian fleet is defeated at Salamis.

title: Warring States period
description: Rival Chinese states fight for supremacy as Zhou royal power fades, while philosophy and military theory flourish.

title: Peloponnesian War
description: Athens and Sparta fight a long war that ends with Athens’ defeat.

title: Conquests of Alexander the Great
description: Alexander of Macedon defeats the Achaemenid Empire and reaches India. He dies in Babylon in 323 BCE.

title: Battle of Ipsus
description: Alexander’s successors fight; Seleucus wins with war elephants and gains Syria.

title: Euclid’s Elements
description: In Alexandria, Euclid writes the Elements, a geometry textbook used for over 2,000 years.

title: First Punic War
description: Rome and Carthage fight for Sicily; Rome wins and takes its first overseas province.

title: Kalinga War and Ashoka’s conversion
description: Horrified by the bloodshed of the Kalinga war, Emperor Ashoka embraces Buddhism and spreads its ideas in edicts across India.

title: Parthian Empire founded
description: Arsaces I leads the Parni into Parthia, founding the Arsacid (Parthian) Empire.

title: Qin unifies China
description: Qin Shi Huang becomes China’s first emperor, standardising writing, money and measures.

title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
description: Hannibal leads a Carthaginian army with war elephants over the Alps into Italy.
source: Wikipedia: Hannibal's crossing of the Alps (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Terracotta Army
description: Qin Shi Huang is buried with an army of thousands of life-sized terracotta soldiers near Xi’an.

title: Modu Chanyu unites the Xiongnu
description: Modu becomes chanyu and builds the Xiongnu into a steppe empire.

title: Han dynasty founded
description: Liu Bang (Emperor Gaozu) wins the civil war after the Qin collapse and founds the Han dynasty.

title: Battle of Baideng
description: The Xiongnu surround the Han founder Liu Bang; the Han agree to pay tribute in a peace deal.

title: Maccabean Revolt
description: A Jewish revolt against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV, remembered at Hanukkah.

title: Destruction of Carthage and Corinth
description: Rome destroys Carthage and Corinth, becoming the dominant Mediterranean power.

title: Zhang Qian opens the Silk Road
description: Han envoy Zhang Qian travels to Central Asia. His missions open the trade routes later called the Silk Road.

title: Battle of Carrhae
description: Parthian horse archers destroy a Roman army under Crassus.

title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
description: Caesar is killed by senators. The civil wars that follow end the Republic.

title: Battle of Actium
description: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra, ending Ptolemaic Egypt and paving the way for the Roman Empire.

title: Augustus becomes first emperor
description: Octavian takes the title Augustus, beginning the Roman Empire and two centuries of Pax Romana.

title: Crucifixion of Jesus
description: Jesus of Nazareth is crucified in Roman Judea (c. 30–33 CE); Christianity grows from his followers.
source: Wikipedia: Jesus (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Vesuvius buries Pompeii
description: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius buries Pompeii and Herculaneum.
source: Wikipedia: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Papermaking refined by Cai Lun
description: The Han court official Cai Lun presents an improved method of making paper.

title: Roman Empire at its greatest extent
description: Under Trajan, the empire reaches its largest size, from Britain to Mesopotamia.

title: Reign of Kanishka
description: Kanishka rules the Kushan Empire at its height and supports Buddhism.
source: Wikipedia: Kanishka (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Antonine Plague
description: An epidemic, possibly smallpox, sweeps the Roman Empire, killing millions.

title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
description: A massive peasant uprising shakes the Han dynasty. Generals who suppress it become warlords.

title: Battle of Red Cliffs
description: Allied forces of Sun Quan and Liu Bei defeat Cao Cao on the Yangtze.

title: End of the Han
description: The last Han emperor abdicates, and China splits into the Three Kingdoms and nearly four centuries of division.

title: Sasanians overthrow the Parthians
description: Ardashir I defeats the last Parthian king, Artabanus IV, and founds the Sasanian Empire.

title: Classic Maya period begins
description: Maya city-states such as Tikal flourish, with monumental temples, writing and astronomy.

title: Lord of Sipán buried
description: A Moche ruler is buried with gold and silver treasures; his tomb was found intact in 1987.
source: Wikipedia: Lord of Sipán (year from general references; not stated in the parts checked checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Jin reunifies China
description: The Jin conquer Eastern Wu, ending the Three Kingdoms period.

title: Sack of Luoyang
description: Han-Zhao forces sack the Jin capital; many northerners flee south.

title: Edict of Milan
description: Emperor Constantine legalises Christianity in the Roman Empire.

title: Constantinople founded
description: Constantine makes Byzantium his new capital, Constantinople.

title: Aksum adopts Christianity
description: King Ezana of Aksum converts to Christianity, one of the first rulers in the world to do so.

title: Decline of Kush and Meroë
description: The Kingdom of Kush breaks apart in the 4th century; Aksum raids Meroë.

title: Teotihuacan intervenes at Tikal
description: Warriors linked to Teotihuacan arrive at Tikal; a new dynasty takes the throne.
source: Wikipedia: Siyaj K'ak' (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Battle of Fei River
description: The Eastern Jin defeat a much larger Former Qin army, keeping the south independent.

title: Visigoths sack Rome
description: Alaric’s Visigoths sack Rome, a deep shock to the Roman world.

title: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
description: Romans and Visigoths stop Attila’s Huns in Gaul.

title: Yungang Grottoes begun
description: The Northern Wei start carving giant Buddhist cave temples near Datong.
source: Wikipedia: Yungang Grottoes (year from general references; not stated in the parts checked checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: Odoacer deposes the last western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, at Ravenna.

title: Aryabhata’s mathematics
description: Aryabhata writes the Aryabhatiya, a landmark work using place-value numbers.

title: Extreme weather of 535–536
description: Volcanic eruptions cause a sudden cold period across the Northern Hemisphere.

title: Hagia Sophia completed
description: Justinian’s great domed church in Constantinople is completed.

title: Plague of Justinian
description: The first recorded bubonic plague pandemic strikes the Byzantine Empire and the Mediterranean world.

title: Teotihuacan’s centre burned
description: The main buildings of Teotihuacan are burned, and the city declines.

title: First Turkic Khaganate founded
description: Bumin overthrows the Rouran and founds the Göktürk empire, the first state to use the name “Türk”.

title: Sui reunify China
description: The Sui dynasty ends nearly four centuries of division.

title: Rise of the Wari Empire
description: The Wari state emerges in the Ayacucho Basin and spreads across Peru.

title: Grand Canal built
description: The Sui build the Grand Canal linking the Yellow River and the Yangtze.

title: Tang dynasty founded
description: Li Yuan founds the Tang, which makes Chang’an one of the greatest cities in the world.

title: Tibetan Empire founded
description: Songtsen Gampo unites Tibet, moves the capital to Lhasa and builds the Tibetan Empire.

title: The Hijra
description: The Prophet Muhammad migrates from Mecca to Medina, the start of the Islamic calendar.

title: Abu Bakr becomes first caliph
description: After Muhammad’s death, Abu Bakr becomes the first caliph of the Rashidun Caliphate.

title: Battle of Yarmouk
description: Arab Muslim forces defeat the Byzantine army, opening Syria to conquest.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of the Yarmuk (year from general references; not stated in the parts checked checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Fall of the Sasanian Empire
description: Arab Muslim armies complete the conquest of Persia.

title: Umayyad Caliphate founded
description: Mu‘awiya I founds the Umayyad dynasty, ruling from Damascus.

title: Kedukan Bukit inscription
description: The Kedukan Bukit inscription (dated 682/683) is the earliest dated inscription of Srivijaya and one of the oldest surviving Malay texts.

title: Umayyad conquest of Iberia
description: Umayyad forces cross from North Africa and conquer most of the Iberian peninsula.
source: Wikipedia: Umayyad conquest of Hispania (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Battle of Tours
description: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeat an Umayyad army in Gaul.

title: Orkhon inscriptions
description: Stone monuments to Kül Tegin and Bilge Khagan, the oldest known texts in a Turkic language.
source: Wikipedia: Orkhon inscriptions (year from general references; not stated in the parts checked checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Uyghur Khaganate founded
description: The Uyghurs overthrow the Second Turkic Khaganate.

title: Abbasid Revolution
description: The Abbasids overthrow the Umayyads at the Battle of the Zab.

title: Battle of Talas
description: Abbasid forces defeat a Tang army in Central Asia, limiting Tang expansion westward.

title: An Lushan Rebellion
description: A devastating rebellion weakens the Tang dynasty.

title: Tibet takes Chang’an
description: The Tibetan army briefly occupies the Tang capital, Chang’an.

title: Viking raid on Lindisfarne
description: Vikings raid the monastery of Lindisfarne, opening the Viking Age in western Europe.
source: Wikipedia: Viking raid on Lindisfarne (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
description: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne Emperor of the Romans in Rome.

title: Borobudur built
description: The great Buddhist monument of Borobudur is built in central Java under the Sailendra dynasty.

title: Khmer Empire founded
description: Jayavarman II declares himself universal monarch, founding the Khmer Empire.

title: House of Wisdom in Baghdad
description: Scholars in Abbasid Baghdad translate and extend Greek, Persian and Indian science, including al-Khwarizmi’s algebra.

title: Fall of the Uyghur Khaganate
description: The Yenisei Kyrgyz destroy the Uyghur capital; Uyghurs move south-west to Gansu and Turfan.

title: Treaty of Verdun
description: Charlemagne’s grandsons divide the Carolingian Empire into three kingdoms.

title: Pagan Kingdom founded
description: Pagan (Bagan) is founded on the Irrawaddy; it later unifies Myanmar.

title: The Diamond Sutra
description: A Buddhist scroll from Dunhuang, the oldest surviving dated printed book.
source: Wikipedia: Diamond Sutra (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Oleg takes Kiev
description: Oleg of Novgorod takes Kiev and makes it the centre of Rus’.
source: Wikipedia: Oleg of Novgorod (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Classic Maya collapse
description: Many southern Maya cities are abandoned in the 9th century, probably due to drought, war and overpopulation.

title: Fatimid Caliphate founded
description: Abd Allah al-Mahdi proclaims the Ismaili Fatimid Caliphate in North Africa.

title: Goryeo founded
description: Wang Kŏn founds Goryeo, which reunifies Korea in 936.

title: Althing founded
description: Icelanders set up the Althing, an open-air assembly and one of the world’s oldest parliaments.
source: Wikipedia: Althing (year from general references; not stated in the parts checked checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Battle of Bạch Đằng
description: Ngô Quyền defeats a Southern Han fleet, ending a thousand years of Chinese rule in Vietnam.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of Bạch Đằng (938) (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Tuʻi Tonga expansion begins
description: Tongan chiefs begin extending their influence across West Polynesia by sea.

title: Holy Roman Empire founded
description: Otto I is crowned emperor in Rome.

title: Cairo founded
description: The Fatimids conquer Egypt and found Cairo.
source: Wikipedia: Cairo (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Sviatoslav sacks Atil
description: Prince Sviatoslav I of Kiev destroys the Khazar capital, ending Khazar power.

title: Christianisation of Rus’
description: Vladimir the Great adopts Orthodox Christianity from Byzantium.
source: Wikipedia: Christianization of Kievan Rus' (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Norse reach North America
description: Norse voyagers build a camp at L’Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland around 1000.

title: Treaty of Chanyuan
description: The Song agree to pay silk and silver to the Liao, starting a century of peace.

title: Brihadisvara Temple completed
description: Rajaraja I completes the great Chola temple at Thanjavur.

title: First government paper money
description: The Song government begins issuing jiaozi paper money in Sichuan.

title: Chola raid on Srivijaya
description: The Chola Empire of South India raids Srivijaya’s ports, weakening its control of the straits.

title: Mahmud of Ghazni raids Somnath
description: Mahmud sacks the Somnath temple in Gujarat, one of many raids into India.

title: Movable-type printing
description: Bi Sheng invents movable type made of fired clay.

title: Battle of Dandanaqan
description: The Seljuks defeat the Ghaznavids and take over Khorasan.

title: Cahokia rises
description: Cahokia grows into the largest city north of Mexico, with Monks Mound at its centre.

title: East–West Schism
description: The Christian churches of Rome and Constantinople formally split.

title: Norman conquest of England
description: William of Normandy defeats Harold II at Hastings.

title: Battle of Stamford Bridge
description: Harald Hardrada of Norway is killed invading England, often seen as the end of the Viking Age.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of Stamford Bridge (year from general references; not stated in the parts checked checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Battle of Manzikert
description: The Seljuks defeat and capture the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement.

title: University of Bologna
description: Traditionally founded in 1088, the oldest university in continuous operation.

title: First Crusade
description: Western European crusaders capture Jerusalem.

title: Crusaders take Jerusalem
description: The First Crusade captures Jerusalem from the Fatimids.

title: Angkor Wat built
description: Suryavarman II builds Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world.

title: Jurchen Jin capture Kaifeng
description: The Jin take the Northern Song capital and two emperors; the Song move south.

title: Saladin ends the Fatimids
description: Saladin abolishes the Fatimid Caliphate and founds the Ayyubid dynasty.
source: Wikipedia: Saladin (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Champa sacks Angkor
description: A Cham fleet sails up the Mekong and sacks the Khmer capital.
source: Wikipedia: Khmer–Cham war (1177–1181) (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Giralda minaret begun
description: The Almohads build the Great Mosque of Seville and its minaret, the Giralda.
source: Wikipedia: Giralda (year from general references; not stated in the parts checked checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Battle of Hattin
description: Saladin defeats the Crusaders and retakes Jerusalem.

title: Genghis Khan unites the Mongols
description: Temujin is proclaimed Genghis Khan, founding the Mongol Empire.

title: Delhi Sultanate founded
description: Qutb ud-Din Aibak rules independently from Delhi, beginning the Delhi Sultanate.

title: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
description: Castile, Aragon and Navarre defeat the Almohads, a turning point in Iberia.

title: Magna Carta
description: English barons force King John to accept limits on royal power.

title: Mongols destroy the Jin
description: The last Jin emperor dies as Caizhou falls to the Mongols and Song.

title: Mongols sack Kiev
description: Batu’s army destroys Kiev, ending Kievan Rus’.

title: Mongols invade Europe
description: Mongol armies defeat Polish and Hungarian forces at Legnica and Mohi.

title: Mamluks take power in Egypt
description: Slave-soldiers overthrow the Ayyubids and found the Mamluk Sultanate.

title: Tripitaka Koreana completed
description: Goryeo finishes carving over 80,000 woodblocks of Buddhist scriptures.

title: Mongols sack Baghdad
description: A Mongol army destroys Baghdad, ending the Abbasid Caliphate there.

title: Maragheh observatory
description: Hulegu founds a great observatory where Nasir al-Din al-Tusi and other scholars work.
source: Wikipedia: Maragheh observatory (year from general references; not stated in the parts checked checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Battle of Ain Jalut
description: The Mamluks defeat a Mongol army in Palestine, halting Mongol expansion.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of Ain Jalut (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Kublai Khan founds the Yuan
description: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty, which conquers the Song by 1279.

title: Travels of Marco Polo
description: The Venetian merchant travels to Kublai Khan’s court; his book shapes European ideas of Asia.

title: Mongol invasions of Japan
description: Two Yuan fleets attack Japan and are wrecked, partly by storms (the “kamikaze”).

title: Mongol invasion of Pagan

description: Trần Hưng Đạo destroys the Yuan fleet at the Bạch Đằng river.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of Bạch Đằng (1288) (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Fall of Acre
description: The Mamluks take Acre, the last major Crusader stronghold.

title: Majapahit founded
description: Raden Wijaya founds Majapahit in East Java after a failed Mongol invasion.

title: Ilkhan Ghazan converts to Islam
description: Ghazan becomes Muslim; the Mongol rulers of Iran adopt Islam.

title: Osman founds the Ottoman state
description: Osman I leads a small Turkish principality in north-western Anatolia that grows into the Ottoman Empire.
source: Wikipedia: Osman I (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Great Enclosure of Great Zimbabwe

title: Mansa Musa’s pilgrimage
description: The ruler of Mali travels to Mecca with so much gold that he affects prices in Cairo.

title: Tenochtitlan founded
description: The Mexica found their island city in Lake Texcoco.

title: Gajah Mada’s Palapa Oath
description: Majapahit’s chief minister vows to unite the archipelago.

description: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I found the Vijayanagara Empire.

description: England and France fight a long series of wars for the French throne.

description: Plague kills perhaps a third to half of Europe’s population, and many people in the Middle East and North Africa.

title: Ayutthaya founded
description: King Uthong founds Ayutthaya, later Siam’s great kingdom.

title: Ming dynasty founded
description: Zhu Yuanzhang drives out the Mongol Yuan and founds the Ming.

title: Timur takes power
description: Timur becomes ruler in Samarkand and begins decades of conquest.

title: Jikji printed with metal type

title: Battle of Ankara
description: Timur defeats and captures the Ottoman sultan Bayezid I.

description: Ulugh Beg builds an observatory in Samarkand with a giant meridian arc.

description: Ayutthaya sacks Angkor, and the Khmer court moves south.

title: Machu Picchu built

description: Johannes Gutenberg develops movable-type printing in Mainz.

description: The Ottoman sultan Mehmed II captures Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire.

title: Inca conquer Chimor
description: Topa Inca Yupanqui conquers the Chimú kingdom and its capital Chan Chan.

title: Đại Việt conquers Vijaya
description: Lê Thánh Tông takes the Cham capital Vijaya; Champa never recovers.

title: Great Stand on the Ugra
description: Muscovy faces down the Great Horde, traditionally the end of Mongol rule over Russia.
source: Wikipedia: Great Stand on the Ugra River (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Columbus reaches the Americas
description: Columbus’s voyage begins sustained contact between Europe and the Americas.

title: Vasco da Gama reaches India
description: Da Gama sails round Africa to Calicut, opening a sea route from Europe to Asia.
source: Wikipedia: Vasco da Gama (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Portuguese capture Melaka
description: A Portuguese fleet under Afonso de Albuquerque captures Melaka after a siege. The sultan’s court withdraws south, eventually founding the Johor Sultanate.

title: Ottomans conquer Mamluk Egypt
description: Selim I defeats the Mamluk Sultanate and takes Cairo, bringing Egypt, Syria and the holy cities of Mecca and Medina under Ottoman rule.

title: Luther’s Ninety-five Theses
description: Martin Luther’s criticism of the sale of indulgences in Wittenberg helps launch the Protestant Reformation, which divides Western Christianity.

title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
description: Spanish forces under Hernán Cortés, with many Indigenous allies, capture the Mexica (Aztec) capital after a siege worsened by a smallpox epidemic.

title: First Battle of Panipat
description: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi of the Delhi Sultanate, using field artillery, and founds the Mughal Empire.

title: Battle of Mohács
description: The Ottoman army under Suleiman I defeats the Kingdom of Hungary; King Louis II dies. Most of Hungary is later divided between the Ottomans and the Habsburgs.

title: First Siege of Vienna
description: Suleiman I besieges Vienna but withdraws as winter approaches. This marks the northwestern limit of Ottoman expansion for a century and a half.

title: Spanish conquest of the Inca
description: Francisco Pizarro captures the Inca ruler Atahualpa at Cajamarca, bringing down the empire.

title: Copernicus: the Sun at the centre
description: Nicolaus Copernicus publishes his theory that the Earth moves around the Sun.
source: Wikipedia: De revolutionibus orbium coelestium (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Silver found at Potosí
description: Huge silver deposits are found at Potosí (in today’s Bolivia). Mined largely with coerced Indigenous labour, this silver flows to Europe and China and changes world trade.

title: Süleymaniye Mosque completed
description: The architect Mimar Sinan completes the Süleymaniye complex in Istanbul, a landmark of classical Ottoman architecture.

title: Manila galleon trade begins
description: Spanish galleons begin crossing the Pacific between Acapulco and Manila, exchanging American silver for Chinese silk and porcelain. The route lasts until 1815.

title: Battle of Talikota
description: The Deccan sultanates defeat Vijayanagara; its capital Hampi is sacked.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of Talikota (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Union of Lublin
description: Poland and Lithuania form the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.

title: Ming rebuild the Great Wall
description: The Ming rebuild the wall in brick and stone. These sections are most of today’s visible Great Wall.

title: Battle of Lepanto
description: A Holy League fleet led by Spain and Venice defeats the Ottoman navy. The Ottomans rebuild their fleet within a year and take Cyprus.

title: Warsaw Confederation
description: The Commonwealth’s nobles guarantee religious tolerance.

title: Battle of Tondibi
description: A Moroccan army equipped with firearms defeats the Songhai army. The Songhai Empire fragments soon afterwards.

title: Imjin War
description: Japanese forces under Toyotomi Hideyoshi invade Korea. Joseon forces, including Admiral Yi Sun-sin’s navy, and Ming Chinese armies resist until Japan withdraws in 1598.

title: Dutch East India Company (VOC) founded
description: The Dutch Republic charters the VOC, an early joint-stock company with powers to wage war and make treaties in Asia.

title: Tokugawa Ieyasu becomes shogun
description: After victory at Sekigahara (1600), Tokugawa Ieyasu is appointed shogun, beginning over 250 years of Tokugawa rule from Edo.

title: Reign of Iskandar Muda of Aceh
description: Sultan Iskandar Muda expands Aceh to control much of the Sumatran pepper trade and parts of the Malay Peninsula, Aceh’s high point.

title: Galileo’s telescope observations
description: In Padua, Galileo Galilei improves the telescope and observes the moons of Jupiter, supporting the Sun-centred model of the solar system.

title: Sultan Agung of Mataram
description: Sultan Agung expands Mataram across most of Java. His sieges of Dutch Batavia (1628–29) fail.

title: Thirty Years’ War
description: A series of wars, mainly fought in the Holy Roman Empire, kills a large share of the population of central Europe. It ends with the Peace of Westphalia (1648).

title: The Vasa sinks
description: Sweden’s new royal warship sinks on its maiden voyage in Stockholm.

title: Battle of Breitenfeld
description: Gustavus Adolphus’ reformed Swedish army wins a major victory in the Thirty Years’ War.

title: Taj Mahal built
description: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan commissions the Taj Mahal in Agra as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

title: Dutch take Melaka from Portugal
description: The VOC, allied with Johor, captures Portuguese Melaka after a long siege.

title: Qing enter Beijing
description: After rebels under Li Zicheng take Beijing and the last Ming emperor dies, Manchu forces enter the city, and the Qing dynasty begins its rule over China.

title: Treaty of Roskilde
description: Denmark–Norway cedes large territories to Sweden, the height of Swedish power.

title: Great Plague of London
description: An outbreak of bubonic plague kills an estimated 75,000–100,000 people in London.

title: Shivaji crowned
description: Shivaji is crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad, founding the Maratha state.

title: Second Siege of Vienna
description: A relief army led by Polish king Jan III Sobieski defeats the Ottoman army besieging Vienna. The Habsburgs go on to regain Hungary.

title: Newton’s Principia
description: Isaac Newton sets out the laws of motion and universal gravitation.
source: Wikipedia: Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Treaty of Nerchinsk
description: Qing China and Russia agree their first border treaty, negotiated with the help of Jesuit interpreters.

title: Treaty of Karlowitz
description: The Ottoman Empire cedes most of Hungary and other lands. It is the first major permanent Ottoman territorial loss in Europe.

title: Asante Empire founded
description: Osei Tutu unites the Akan states under the Golden Stool and defeats Denkyira.

title: Acts of Union
description: The kingdoms of England and Scotland unite to form the Kingdom of Great Britain.

title: Battle of Poltava
description: Peter the Great destroys Charles XII’s army, ending Sweden’s great-power era.

title: Peter the Great moves the capital
description: Peter I makes St Petersburg Russia’s capital as part of his westernising reforms. He takes the title of Emperor in 1721.

title: Siege of Isfahan
description: Afghan forces capture the Safavid capital Isfahan after a long siege. Safavid rule collapses; Nader Shah formally ends the dynasty in 1736.

title: First Ottoman Turkish printed book
description: İbrahim Müteferrika’s press, approved after his 1726 petition, publishes the first book printed in Ottoman Turkish.

title: Battle of Plassey
description: The British East India Company defeats the Nawab of Bengal, starting its rise to territorial power in India.

title: Canton System begins
description: The Qing court limits Western maritime trade to Guangzhou (Canton), under licensed merchant houses.

title: Third Battle of Panipat
description: The Durrani Afghans defeat the Marathas in one of the largest battles of the 18th century.
source: Wikipedia: Third Battle of Panipat (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Fall of Ayutthaya
description: Burmese forces sack Ayutthaya, ending the kingdom. Taksin reunifies Siam; the Chakri dynasty founds Bangkok in 1782.

title: Watt’s steam engine
description: James Watt’s improved steam engine, built with Matthew Boulton in Birmingham, becomes a driver of the Industrial Revolution.

title: US Declaration of Independence
description: Thirteen British colonies in North America declare independence in Philadelphia, founding the United States.

title: French Revolution
description: The storming of the Bastille in Paris begins a revolution that abolishes the monarchy (1792) and spreads ideas of popular sovereignty and rights.

title: Haitian Revolution
description: Enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue rise up, leading to the independence of Haiti in 1804, the first state founded after a successful revolt by enslaved people.

title: Constitution of 3 May 1791
description: The Commonwealth adopts a modern written constitution.

title: Macartney embassy
description: A British embassy reaches the Qianlong emperor at Chengde and asks for wider trade rights. The requests are refused.

title: Third Partition of Poland
description: Russia, Prussia and Austria divide the remaining lands of the Commonwealth.
source: Wikipedia: Third Partition of Poland (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: First smallpox vaccine
description: Edward Jenner tests cowpox inoculation against smallpox, the basis of vaccination.

title: Ranjit Singh takes Lahore
description: Ranjit Singh captures Lahore, founding the Sikh Empire.

title: Nguyen dynasty founded
description: Gia Long unifies Vietnam and founds the Nguyen dynasty with its capital at Huế.

title: Spanish American wars of independence
description: Led by figures such as Simón Bolívar and José de San Martín, most of Spain’s American colonies win independence.
source: Wikipedia: Spanish American wars of independence

title: Kamehameha I unifies Hawaiʻi
description: Kauaʻi and Niʻihau join the kingdom, completing the unification of the islands.

title: Mount Tambora erupts
description: The largest volcanic eruption in recorded history, on Sumbawa, kills tens of thousands locally and causes the “Year Without a Summer” (1816) worldwide.

title: Waterloo and the Congress of Vienna
description: Napoleon is finally defeated at Waterloo. The Congress of Vienna redraws the map of Europe and begins a long period of great-power balance.

title: Shaka becomes Zulu king
description: Shaka takes power and reforms the Zulu army.

title: Fall of the Maratha Confederacy
description: The British East India Company defeats the Peshwa in the Third Anglo-Maratha War.

title: British trading post at Singapore
description: Stamford Raffles sets up a British trading post at Singapore by an agreement with a Johor claimant and the local Temenggong.

title: Brazil declares independence
description: Prince Pedro declares Brazil’s independence from Portugal and becomes Emperor Pedro I.

title: Anglo-Dutch Treaty
description: Britain and the Netherlands divide their spheres in the Malay world along the Strait of Melaka, splitting the Johor-Riau realm.

title: First public steam railway
description: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opens in England, beginning the railway age.

title: Java War
description: Prince Diponegoro leads a major uprising against Dutch colonial rule in Java. It ends with his capture.

title: Straits Settlements formed
description: Penang, Melaka and Singapore are grouped as the British Straits Settlements.

title: French invasion of Algiers
description: France captures Algiers. This begins the second French colonial empire and a long, violent conquest of Algeria.

title: Slavery Abolition Act
description: Britain abolishes slavery across most of its empire, with compensation paid to slave owners, not to the enslaved.

title: First Opium War
description: Britain goes to war with Qing China after China moves against the opium trade. The Treaty of Nanjing (1842) cedes Hong Kong Island and opens five treaty ports.

title: Tanzimat reforms begin
description: The Edict of Gülhane launches Ottoman reforms aimed at legal equality, centralisation and modern administration.

title: Great Famine in Ireland
description: Potato blight and government policy combine to cause about one million deaths and mass emigration from Ireland.

title: Revolutions of 1848
description: A wave of liberal and national revolutions sweeps Europe. Most are suppressed, but serfdom ends in the Habsburg lands. Marx and Engels publish The Communist Manifesto.

title: Britain annexes the Punjab
description: After the Second Anglo-Sikh War, the Sikh Empire is annexed.

title: Taiping Rebellion
description: A religious-political movement captures Nanjing and much of southern China. It is one of the deadliest conflicts of the 19th century, with tens of millions of deaths (estimates vary).

title: Perry’s ships arrive in Japan
description: US Commodore Matthew Perry’s squadron forces Tokugawa Japan to open ports to trade (Treaty of Kanagawa, 1854).

title: Indian Rebellion of 1857
description: A widespread uprising against East India Company rule. Afterwards the last Mughal emperor is exiled and the British Crown takes direct control of India.

title: French conquest of Cochinchina
description: French and Spanish forces attack Đà Nẵng and Saigon. By the Treaty of Saigon (1862) the Nguyễn court cedes southern provinces to France.

title: On the Origin of Species
description: Charles Darwin publishes his theory of evolution by natural selection.

title: Emancipation of the Russian serfs
description: Alexander II frees about 23 million serfs, the largest reform in Russian history.

title: Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
description: Most of the Italian peninsula is unified under the House of Savoy (Rome follows in 1870).

title: American Civil War
description: Eleven Southern states secede over slavery. After the Union victory slavery is abolished (Thirteenth Amendment, 1865).

title: Paraguayan War
description: Paraguay fights Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay. It is among the deadliest wars in Latin American history: an estimated 150,000–500,000 dead in total, and Paraguay lost a very large share of its population (exact numbers are disputed).

title: Mendel founds genetics
description: Gregor Mendel publishes his pea-plant experiments, the basis of modern genetics.
source: Wikipedia: Experiments on Plant Hybridization (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
description: The Habsburg monarchy becomes the dual monarchy of Austria-Hungary.

title: Meiji Restoration
description: The Tokugawa shogunate ends and imperial rule is restored under Emperor Meiji, followed by rapid industrialisation and reform.

title: Suez Canal opens
description: The canal links the Mediterranean and Red Sea, shortening the sea route between Europe and Asia.

title: German Empire proclaimed
description: After the Franco-Prussian War, the German Empire is proclaimed at Versailles with the Prussian king as emperor.

title: Aceh War
description: The Netherlands wages a long war to conquer the Aceh Sultanate, which resists for decades.

title: Treaty of Pangkor
description: The treaty places a British Resident in Perak, beginning British indirect rule over the Malay states.

title: The telephone
description: Alexander Graham Bell patents the telephone in the United States.

title: Battle of Isandlwana
description: A Zulu army defeats a British force in the Anglo-Zulu War.

title: Practical electric light
description: Thomas Edison’s team and others produce long-lasting incandescent light bulbs.
source: Wikipedia: Incandescent light bulb (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Krakatoa eruption
description: The eruption of Krakatoa and the tsunamis it caused kill at least 36,417 people in the Dutch East Indies. Ash cools the global climate.

title: Berlin Conference
description: European powers set rules for claiming African territory, speeding up the colonial “Scramble for Africa”.

title: Brazil abolishes slavery
description: The Golden Law ends slavery in Brazil, the last country in the Americas to do so. The monarchy falls the next year.

title: Brunei becomes a British protectorate
description: The Sultanate of Brunei, having lost Sarawak and North Borneo, becomes a British protectorate.

title: Franco-Siamese crisis
description: French gunboats force their way to Bangkok. Siam cedes territory east of the Mekong (in Laos) to France but keeps its independence.

title: Overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom
description: Queen Liliʻuokalani is overthrown by a group backed by US forces; annexation follows in 1898.

title: First Sino-Japanese War
description: Japan defeats Qing China. China recognises Korean independence and cedes Taiwan to Japan.

title: Federated Malay States
description: Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang are joined as the Federated Malay States, with Kuala Lumpur as capital.

title: Radio
description: Guglielmo Marconi develops practical radio communication.
source: Wikipedia: Guglielmo Marconi (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Battle of Adwa
description: Ethiopian forces under Emperor Menelik II defeat an Italian army, preserving Ethiopian independence.

title: British expedition to Benin
description: British forces take Benin City and loot thousands of artworks, the Benin Bronzes.

title: Spanish–American War
description: The US defeats Spain. Spain loses Cuba, Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines, ending its American empire.

title: Boxer Rebellion
description: An anti-foreign and anti-Christian uprising in northern China is crushed by an eight-nation alliance. China is forced to pay huge indemnities.

title: War of the Golden Stool
description: Asante resistance led by Yaa Asantewaa after a British demand for the Golden Stool.
source: Wikipedia: War of the Golden Stool (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: First powered flight
description: The Wright brothers make the first controlled, powered aeroplane flight at Kitty Hawk.

title: Russo-Japanese War
description: Japan defeats Russia over Manchuria and Korea, the first major victory of an Asian power over a European one in modern times.

title: Herero and Nama genocide
description: German colonial forces in South West Africa (Namibia) kill tens of thousands of Herero and Nama people, often described as the first genocide of the 20th century.

title: Theory of relativity
description: Albert Einstein publishes special relativity and other landmark papers while working in Bern.

title: Persian Constitutional Revolution
description: Protests force the Qajar shah to accept a constitution and an elected parliament (Majlis).

title: Japan annexes Korea
description: Japan formally annexes Korea, beginning 35 years of colonial rule.

title: Xinhai Revolution
description: An uprising in Wuchang spreads across China. The last Qing emperor abdicates in 1912, and the Republic of China is founded.

title: First World War
description: A global war centred in Europe. The German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman empires collapse during or after it.

title: Assassination in Sarajevo
description: Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to Austria-Hungary, is assassinated, triggering the crisis that starts the First World War.
source: Wikipedia: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand

title: Armenian genocide
description: The Ottoman government deports and systematically kills its Armenian population. Estimates are 600,000–1.5 million dead. Almost all historians accept it as genocide; the Turkish government disputes this description.

title: Russian Revolutions
description: The tsar abdicates in February. The Bolsheviks take power in October, leading to civil war and the founding of the Soviet Union (1922).

title: 1918 influenza pandemic
description: A global influenza pandemic kills an estimated 17–50 million people or more.

title: Treaty of Versailles
description: The peace treaty ending the First World War imposes territorial losses and reparations on Germany. The League of Nations is created.

title: May Fourth Movement
description: Student protests in Beijing against the Versailles settlement launch a movement for Chinese nationalism and cultural modernisation.

title: Republic of Turkey founded
description: After the Turkish War of Independence, the Republic of Turkey is proclaimed in Ankara under Mustafa Kemal (Atatürk).

title: Treaty of Lausanne
description: The treaty recognises the borders of the new Republic of Turkey and includes a population exchange between Greece and Turkey.

title: Penicillin discovered
description: Alexander Fleming notices the antibacterial effect of the Penicillium mould in London. Mass production follows in the 1940s.

title: Turkish alphabet reform
description: Atatürk’s government replaces the Arabic script with the Latin alphabet, one of many secularising reforms.

title: Great Depression
description: The Wall Street Crash begins a worldwide economic slump that hits trade, commodity prices and employment.

title: Gandhi’s Salt March
description: Gandhi leads a 24-day march to Dandi to make salt in defiance of British law, a landmark of non-violent resistance.

title: Mukden Incident
description: Japanese officers stage an explosion as a pretext to invade Manchuria, where Japan sets up the puppet state of Manchukuo.

title: Siamese revolution of 1932
description: A bloodless coup ends absolute monarchy in Siam and creates a constitutional monarchy. The country is renamed Thailand in 1939.

title: Holodomor and the Soviet famine
description: Famine in the Soviet Union, made far worse by forced collectivisation and grain requisitions, kills an estimated 3.5–5 million people in Ukraine and many others, especially in Kazakhstan. Whether it constitutes genocide is disputed; Ukraine and over 30 other states recognise it as such.

title: Nazis take power in Germany
description: Adolf Hitler becomes chancellor and quickly turns Germany into a one-party dictatorship.
source: Wikipedia: Adolf Hitler’s rise to power

title: Long March
description: The Chinese Communists retreat about 10,000 km from Nationalist forces. Mao Zedong emerges as leader.

title: Nanjing Massacre
description: After capturing Nanjing, Japanese troops kill large numbers of civilians and prisoners and commit mass rape. Death toll estimates vary widely.

title: Second World War
description: The deadliest conflict in history, fought in Europe, Asia, Africa and the Pacific, with an estimated 70–85 million deaths.

title: The Holocaust
description: Nazi Germany murders around six million European Jews, as well as millions of others including Roma, Poles, Soviet prisoners of war, disabled people and gay men. Auschwitz-Birkenau was the largest killing centre.

title: Japanese invasion and occupation of Malaya
description: Japanese troops land at Kota Bharu on 8 December 1941. Singapore surrenders on 15 February 1942, beginning over three years of occupation.
source: Wikipedia: Japanese occupation of Malaya (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Battle of Stalingrad
description: One of the deadliest battles in history ends with the destruction of a German army, a turning point of the war in Europe.

title: Bengal famine of 1943
description: An estimated 800,000 to 3.8 million people die in Bengal under British rule during wartime. Historians debate how much was caused by wartime policies versus other factors.

title: D-Day landings
description: Allied forces land in Normandy, opening a western front against Nazi Germany.

title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
description: The United States drops atomic bombs on two Japanese cities. Japan surrenders shortly afterwards.

title: Indonesian independence
description: Sukarno and Hatta proclaim independence in Jakarta. The Netherlands recognises Indonesian sovereignty in 1949 after armed and diplomatic struggle.

title: United Nations founded
description: The UN Charter is signed in San Francisco to preserve peace after the Second World War.

title: Chinese Civil War (final phase)
description: After Japan’s defeat, the Communists defeat the Nationalists, who retreat to Taiwan in 1949.

title: ENIAC, an early computer
description: The first programmable, electronic, general-purpose digital computer is completed.

title: Malayan Union
description: Britain creates the Malayan Union (1 April 1946). Strong Malay opposition, which led to the founding of UMNO, brings its replacement by the Federation of Malaya in 1948.

title: Independence and Partition of India
description: British India becomes independent as India and Pakistan. Partition causes mass migration and violence.

title: Partition violence and migration
description: The partition of British India displaces 12–20 million people. Estimates of deaths range from 200,000 to 2 million.

title: The transistor
description: Scientists at Bell Labs build the first transistor, the building block of modern electronics.
source: Wikipedia: Transistor (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Malayan Emergency
description: The Malayan Communist Party wages a guerrilla war against British and then Malayan forces. It is defeated by 1960.

title: Founding of Israel and the Nakba
description: The State of Israel is declared and the first Arab–Israeli war follows. Around 750,000 Palestinians are expelled or flee their homes, known to Palestinians as the Nakba (“catastrophe”).

title: Apartheid in South Africa
description: South Africa’s government introduces apartheid, a system of legal racial segregation and white minority rule.

title: People’s Republic of China proclaimed
description: After the civil war, Mao Zedong proclaims the PRC in Beijing. The ROC government relocates to Taiwan.

title: Korean War
description: North Korea invades South Korea. UN forces led by the US and Chinese forces join in. A ceasefire is signed on 27 July 1953, leaving Korea divided. Millions of soldiers and civilians die.

title: India becomes a republic
description: India’s constitution comes into force, making it the world’s largest democracy.

title: 1953 coup in Iran
description: A coup backed by the US and UK overthrows Prime Minister Mosaddegh after he nationalised the oil industry, strengthening the Shah.

title: The structure of DNA
description: The double-helix structure of DNA is published, using X-ray data from Rosalind Franklin’s group.
source: Wikipedia: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Bandung Conference
description: Leaders of 29 Asian and African countries meet in Indonesia, a founding moment for the Non-Aligned Movement.

title: Vietnam War
description: North Vietnam and the Viet Cong fight South Vietnam and the United States. It ends with the fall of Saigon on 30 April 1975. Vietnamese deaths are estimated at about 1–3 million.

title: Suez Crisis
description: Britain, France and Israel invade Egypt after it nationalises the Suez Canal. US and Soviet pressure forces them to withdraw.

title: Malayan independence
description: The Federation of Malaya becomes independent from Britain. Malaysia is formed in 1963 with Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore (which leaves in 1965).

title: Sputnik 1
description: The Soviet Union launches the first artificial satellite from Baikonur, opening the Space Age.

title: Ghana’s independence
description: Ghana becomes one of the first sub-Saharan African colonies to win independence, under Kwame Nkrumah.

title: Great Chinese Famine
description: Policies of the Great Leap Forward and natural factors lead to a famine with tens of millions of deaths (estimates vary widely).

title: The Year of Africa
description: 17 African colonies become independent in a single year: 14 from France, 2 from Britain and 1 from Belgium.

title: First human in space
description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbits the Earth.

title: Berlin Wall built
description: East Germany builds a wall around West Berlin, a symbol of the Cold War division of Europe.

title: Algerian independence
description: After an eight-year war, Algeria becomes independent from France.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
description: A 13-day standoff over Soviet missiles in Cuba brings the world close to nuclear war.

title: Formation of Malaysia
description: Malaya, Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak form Malaysia on 16 September 1963.

title: Konfrontasi
description: Indonesia opposes the formation of Malaysia with an undeclared conflict, mostly on Borneo (20 January 1963 – 11 August 1966).

title: Singapore leaves Malaysia
description: Singapore separates from Malaysia and becomes an independent country on 9 August 1965.

title: Indonesia’s 1965–66 killings
description: After an attempted coup, an army-led anti-communist purge kills over half a million people, and Suharto rises to power.

title: Cultural Revolution
description: Mao launches a mass political campaign. Persecution, violence and chaos cause hundreds of thousands to millions of deaths and great cultural destruction.

title: ASEAN founded
description: Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand sign the Bangkok Declaration creating ASEAN.

title: Six-Day War
description: A war between Israel and Egypt, Syria and Jordan (5–10 June 1967); Israel takes the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai and the Golan Heights.

title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
description: US astronauts land on the Moon, launched from Cape Canaveral.

title: 13 May incident
description: Sino-Malay riots in Kuala Lumpur after the general election. Official sources cited 196 deaths; other sources suggest about 600 to over 1,000. A state of emergency and the Rukun Negara followed.

title: New Economic Policy
description: Malaysia launches the New Economic Policy to reduce poverty and restructure the economy along ethnic lines, a policy that remains debated.

title: 1973 oil crisis
description: An Arab oil embargo quadruples oil prices, shaking the world economy.

title: Cambodian genocide
description: The Khmer Rouge regime kills an estimated 1.2–2.2 million Cambodians through executions, forced labour and starvation.

title: Indonesian occupation of East Timor
description: Indonesia invades East Timor in 1975. After a UN-supervised vote in 1999 the territory becomes independent as Timor-Leste in 2002.
source: Wikipedia: Indonesian occupation of East Timor

title: China’s reform and opening-up
description: Under Deng Xiaoping, China begins market reforms, including special economic zones such as Shenzhen.

title: Iranian Revolution
description: Mass protests end the Pahlavi monarchy, and an Islamic Republic is established.

title: Soviet–Afghan War
description: Soviet troops intervene in Afghanistan and fight a long war against mujahideen fighters.

title: Smallpox eradicated
description: The World Health Organization certifies smallpox eradicated, the first human disease wiped out.

title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
description: A reactor explosion in Soviet Ukraine releases radioactive material across Europe.

title: World Wide Web proposed
description: Tim Berners-Lee proposes the World Wide Web at CERN near Geneva.

title: Tiananmen Square protests
description: Mass pro-democracy protests in Beijing end on 3–4 June 1989 when troops open fire. Death toll estimates range from several hundred to the low thousands.
source: Wikipedia: 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre (checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: East Germany opens the Berlin Wall, and communist regimes across Eastern Europe fall.
source: Wikipedia: Fall of the Berlin Wall

title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
description: The Soviet Union dissolves into 15 independent states.

title: European Union created
description: The Maastricht Treaty creates the European Union. The euro follows in 1999.

title: Oslo Accords
description: Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization sign interim agreements (1993, 1995).

title: End of apartheid
description: Nelson Mandela becomes South Africa’s first democratically elected president after the first all-race elections.

title: Rwandan genocide
description: Between April and July 1994, Hutu extremists kill an estimated 500,000–662,000 Tutsi, as well as Twa and moderate Hutu.

title: Asian financial crisis
description: A currency crisis starting in Thailand spreads to Indonesia, Malaysia, South Korea and beyond.

title: Hong Kong handover
description: Britain transfers Hong Kong to the People’s Republic of China, often seen as the symbolic end of the British Empire.

title: Reformasi in Indonesia
description: The Asian financial crisis and mass protests force Suharto to resign on 21 May 1998, opening Indonesia’s transition to democracy.

title: September 11 attacks
description: Al-Qaeda attacks in New York and Washington kill nearly 3,000 people, leading to the US-led wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.

title: Iraq War
description: A US-led coalition invades Iraq in March 2003; the conflict lasts until 2011.

title: Human genome sequenced
description: The international Human Genome Project completes its map of human DNA.

title: Indian Ocean tsunami
description: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra triggers a tsunami that kills about 230,000 people in 14 countries, with Aceh worst hit.

title: The smartphone era
description: The launch of the iPhone (2007) and Android phones puts the internet in billions of pockets.

title: Global financial crisis
description: The collapse of the US housing bubble and of Lehman Brothers triggers the worst global recession since the 1930s.

title: Arab Spring
description: Protests beginning in Tunisia spread across the Arab world, toppling several governments and leading to civil wars in Syria, Libya and Yemen.

title: Syrian civil war
description: Protests against the Assad government in 2011 turn into a long civil war (2011–2024).

title: Higgs boson found
description: CERN physicists announce the discovery of the Higgs boson.
source: Wikipedia: Higgs boson (year from general references; not stated in the summary checked 6 Nov 2026)

title: Paris climate agreement
description: Almost every country agrees to limit global warming to well below 2°C.

title: Malaysia’s 2018 election
description: For the first time since independence, the ruling coalition loses a general election, after the 1MDB scandal.

title: COVID-19 pandemic
description: A coronavirus pandemic, first identified in Wuhan in late 2019, spreads worldwide, causing millions of deaths and major economic disruption.

title: Brexit
description: The United Kingdom leaves the European Union on 31 January 2020.

title: Russian invasion of Ukraine
description: Russia launches a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the largest war in Europe since 1945.

title: Generative AI goes mainstream
description: ChatGPT is released on 30 November 2022, bringing AI chatbots to hundreds of millions of people.

title: Turkey–Syria earthquakes
description: Major earthquakes strike southern Turkey and northern Syria, killing about 59,000–62,000 people.

title: Gaza war
description: The war begins on 7 October 2023 with a Hamas-led attack on Israel, followed by an Israeli military campaign in Gaza; it causes very heavy loss of life and a humanitarian crisis.

title: Budj Bim eel traps
description: The Gunditjmara people build channels and weirs to farm eels, one of the world’s oldest aquaculture systems (now a World Heritage Site).

title: First Fleet arrives at Sydney Cove
description: British ships land convicts and marines at Sydney Cove, beginning the colonisation of Aboriginal Australia. Governor Phillip claims everything east of 135°E as New South Wales, though settlers only held the area around Sydney and Aboriginal nations still lived across almost all of it.

title: Durrani Empire founded
description: Ahmad Shah Durrani is chosen as leader at Kandahar, founding the state that became Afghanistan.

title: Shakushain’s revolt
description: Ainu led by Shakushain rise against the Matsumae clan’s control of trade in Hokkaido; the revolt is defeated.

title: The green Sahara dries up
description: The last “green Sahara” period ends; lakes and grassland turn to desert and herders move to oases and river valleys.

title: Marajoara culture flourishes
description: On Marajó Island at the mouth of the Amazon, people build earth mounds and make elaborately painted pottery.

title: Chaco Canyon at its height
description: Ancestral Puebloans build multi-storey great houses and straight roads around Chaco Canyon.
source: Wikipedia: Chaco Culture National Historical Park

title: Watson Brake mounds built
description: Hunter-gatherers in Louisiana build a ring of earth mounds, among the oldest in the Americas.

title: Thule migration across the Arctic
description: Thule whale hunters, ancestors of the Inuit, spread rapidly from Alaska east to Greenland.

title: Argentine independence declared
description: The Congress of Tucumán declares independence from Spain on 9 July 1816.

title: Falklands War
description: Argentina occupies the Falkland Islands (Malvinas); Britain retakes them after a ten-week war.

title: Australian Federation
description: Six British colonies unite as the Commonwealth of Australia on 1 January 1901.

title: Gallipoli landing
description: Australian and New Zealand troops land at Gallipoli in a failed campaign; 25 April is remembered as Anzac Day.

title: Austronesian expansion begins
description: Seafaring farmers begin spreading from Taiwan into the Philippines and later across the Pacific and Indian Oceans.

title: Baekje sends Buddhism to Japan
description: King Seong of Baekje sends Buddhist images and texts to the Yamato court (traditional date 552, or 538).

title: Fall of Baekje
description: Silla and Tang China conquer Baekje.

title: Bantu expansion under way
description: Farmers speaking Bantu languages spread from the Cameroon–Nigeria area across central and southern Africa.

title: Bolivia becomes independent
description: Upper Peru declares independence and takes the name Bolivia after Simón Bolívar.

title: Chaco War
description: Bolivia and Paraguay fight over the Gran Chaco (1932–35); Bolivia loses most of the disputed land.

title: Brazilian Republic proclaimed
description: Army officers overthrow Emperor Pedro II and proclaim a republic.

title: Brasília becomes the capital
description: The planned city of Brasília is inaugurated as Brazil’s new capital.

title: Lapa do Santo
description: Early people in Minas Gerais leave burials and rock art, some of the oldest in the Americas.

title: Early chariots at Sintashta
description: Burials of the Sintashta culture in the southern Urals contain some of the earliest spoked-wheel chariots.

title: Canadian Confederation
description: Three British colonies unite as the Dominion of Canada on 1 July 1867.

title: Canadian Pacific Railway completed
description: The last spike is driven, linking eastern Canada to British Columbia.

title: Farmers reach the Congo rainforest
description: Bantu-speaking farmers move into the rainforest, beginning long exchange with forest hunter-gatherers.

title: Shaybani takes Samarkand and Bukhara
description: Muhammad Shaybani’s Uzbeks take the Timurid cities, founding the Bukhara khanate.

title: Russia takes Tashkent
description: Russian forces capture Tashkent, beginning the conquest of the Central Asian khanates.

title: Chagatai receives his ulus
description: After Genghis Khan’s death, his son Chagatai rules Central Asia, forming the Chagatai Khanate.

title: Chavín de Huántar New Temple
description: The temple complex at Chavín de Huántar is enlarged, a pilgrimage centre for much of Peru.

title: Chilean independence
description: Chile declares independence after the Battle of Chacabuco and confirms it at Maipú (1818).

title: Valdivia earthquake
description: The strongest earthquake ever recorded (magnitude 9.5) strikes southern Chile.

title: Battle of Boyacá
description: Bolívar’s army defeats Spanish forces, securing the independence of New Granada (Colombia).

title: Colombian peace agreement
description: The government and FARC guerrillas sign a peace agreement after more than 50 years of conflict.

title: Trypillia mega-sites
description: Settlements such as Talianki in Ukraine grow to over 300 hectares, among the largest in the world at the time.

title: Sultanate of Darfur founded
description: Sulayman Solongdungu founds the Keira sultanate of the Fur people.

title: Kalmar Union
description: Queen Margaret I unites Denmark, Norway and Sweden under one king at Kalmar.

title: Congo Free State created
description: Belgian King Leopold II gains the Congo as his personal colony; forced labour for rubber causes mass deaths.

title: Congo becomes independent
description: The Belgian Congo gains independence with Patrice Lumumba as prime minister.

title: Bronze at Ban Chiang
description: Rice farmers in north-east Thailand begin casting bronze.

title: Hopewell earthworks
description: Peoples of the Ohio valley build great geometric earthworks and trade goods across the continent.

title: Haudenosaunee Confederacy formed
description: Five nations unite under the Great Law of Peace (the date is debated, between about 1142 and 1600).

title: Chogha Zanbil ziggurat built
description: King Untash-Napirisha builds a great ziggurat near Susa.

title: Assyria sacks Susa
description: Ashurbanipal destroys the Elamite capital Susa.

title: Hungarians settle the Carpathian Basin
description: Magyar tribes, speakers of a Finno-Ugric language, settle in present-day Hungary.
source: Wikipedia: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin

title: Bulgaria converts to Christianity
description: Khan Boris I is baptised; Bulgaria becomes Christian and later adopts the Cyrillic script.

title: Fifth Republic founded
description: A new constitution led by Charles de Gaulle creates the French Fifth Republic.

title: May 1968 protests
description: Student protests and general strikes shake France.

title: Óc Eo, port of Funan
description: The port of Óc Eo trades goods from India, China and Rome.

title: German reunification
description: East and West Germany reunite on 3 October 1990.

title: Al-Bakri describes Ghana
description: The Andalusian geographer al-Bakri describes the gold-rich Ghana Empire and its capital.

title: Gwanggaeto Stele
description: A great stone records the conquests of King Gwanggaeto of Goguryeo.

title: Fall of Goguryeo
description: Silla and Tang forces capture Pyongyang and end Goguryeo.

title: Ibn Khaldun writes the Muqaddimah
description: The Tunis-born scholar explains the rise and fall of dynasties.

title: Muhammad Rumfa rules Kano
description: Kano grows into a great trading city under Muhammad Rumfa (1463–99).

title: Khajuraho temples
description: The Chandela kings build richly carved Hindu and Jain temples.

title: Kanem’s ruler converts to Islam
description: King Hummay of Kanem adopts Islam.

title: Kazakh Khanate founded
description: Kerei and Janibek break from the Uzbek Khanate and found the Kazakh Khanate.

title: Fire-stick farming
description: Aboriginal Australians manage the land with planned burning to encourage plants and game, a practice used for thousands of years.

title: Sannai-Maruyama village
description: A large Jōmon settlement in northern Japan with big wooden buildings, lasting about 1,500 years.

title: Dutch settle at the Cape
description: The Dutch East India Company sets up a station at the Cape; Khoekhoe herders soon lose grazing land and suffer epidemics.

title: Kilwa at its height
description: Kilwa controls the gold trade from Sofala; its Great Mosque and Husuni Kubwa palace are built of coral stone.

title: Danish constitution
description: Denmark becomes a constitutional monarchy with an elected parliament.

title: Second Schleswig War
description: Prussia and Austria defeat Denmark, which loses Schleswig and Holstein.

title: Alaungpaya reunites Burma
description: Alaungpaya founds the Konbaung dynasty and reunites Burma.

title: First Anglo-Burmese War
description: Britain defeats Burma (1824–26), which loses Assam, Arakan and Tenasserim.

title: Lan Xang founded
description: Fa Ngum founds the kingdom of Lan Xang, “a million elephants”.

title: Lunda Empire expands
description: The Lunda kingdom spreads its system of rule across the southern savanna.

title: Settlers reach Madagascar
description: Austronesian sailors from Borneo, later joined by Africans, settle Madagascar.

title: Andrianampoinimerina unites Merina
description: The king unites the Merina highlands; his son Radama I expands across the island.

title: Baqt treaty
description: After the Second Battle of Dongola, Makuria and Muslim Egypt agree a treaty that lasts about 600 years.

title: Ternate expels the Portuguese
description: Sultan Baabullah drives the Portuguese from Ternate in the Maluku spice islands.

title: Treaty of Waitangi
description: Māori chiefs and the British Crown sign a treaty whose meaning is still debated.

title: Mexican independence
description: After a war begun in 1810, Mexico wins independence from Spain.

title: Mexican Revolution
description: A revolution against Porfirio Díaz leads to a decade of war and the 1917 constitution.

title: Muhammad Ali rules Egypt
description: Muhammad Ali takes power and begins modernising Egypt’s army and economy.

title: Tokyo Olympics and bullet train
description: Japan hosts the Olympics and opens the Shinkansen, symbols of its post-war recovery.

title: Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami
description: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake and tsunami kill about 18,000 people and cause the Fukushima nuclear disaster.

title: Mongolia declares independence
description: Outer Mongolia declares independence from the Qing under the Bogd Khan.

title: Mongolian democratic revolution
description: Peaceful protests end one-party rule.

title: Moulay Ismail builds Meknes
description: Sultan Moulay Ismail makes Meknes his imperial capital.

title: Moroccan independence
description: Morocco regains independence from France and Spain.

title: Battle of Kulikovo
description: Dmitry Donskoy of Moscow defeats a Golden Horde army.

title: Ivan IV crowned tsar
description: Ivan the Terrible becomes the first crowned Tsar of Russia.

title: Nanzhao unified
description: Piluoge unites six kingdoms around Erhai Lake into Nanzhao.

title: Heian-kyō becomes the capital
description: Emperor Kanmu moves the capital to Heian-kyō (Kyoto).

title: The Tale of Genji
description: Murasaki Shikibu writes The Tale of Genji, often called the first novel.

title: Nazca Lines drawn
description: The Nazca draw huge lines and animal figures on the desert.

title: Farming reaches Europe
description: Farmers from Anatolia bring wheat, barley and livestock to Greece and the Balkans.

title: Bahrey describes the Oromo
description: The monk Bahrey writes the first known account of the Oromo and their Gadaa system.

title: Fall of Oyo-Ile
description: The Oyo capital is abandoned after revolts and Fulani attacks.

title: Vikramashila founded
description: Pala king Dharmapala founds the Buddhist university of Vikramashila.

title: Farming begins at Kuk Swamp
description: People in the New Guinea highlands start draining land to grow plants, an independent invention of farming.

title: Peru declares independence
description: José de San Martín declares Peru independent in Lima.

title: War of the Pacific
description: Chile defeats Peru and Bolivia (1879–84) and takes the nitrate-rich desert.

title: People Power Revolution
description: Mass protests in Manila end Ferdinand Marcos’s rule.

title: Horses reach the Plains
description: Horses from Spanish New Mexico spread north, transforming Plains life.

title: Battle of the Little Bighorn
description: Lakota and Cheyenne warriors defeat Custer’s US cavalry.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of the Little Bighorn

title: Union of Krewo
description: Grand Duke Jogaila agrees to marry Queen Jadwiga of Poland and convert Lithuania to Christianity.

title: Battle of Grunwald
description: Poland and Lithuania defeat the Teutonic Knights.

title: Great Dam of Ma’rib
description: The kingdom of Saba builds a great dam to irrigate the desert.

title: Petra flourishes
description: The Nabataeans carve their capital Petra into the rock.

title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
description: A Venetian-led crusade sacks Constantinople; Venice gains ports across the eastern Mediterranean.

title: Fall of the Republic of Venice
description: Napoleon ends the 1,100-year-old Venetian Republic.
source: Wikipedia: Fall of the Republic of Venice

title: Pact of Diriyah
description: Muhammad bin Saud allies with the preacher Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab.

title: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia founded
description: Ibn Saud unites his lands as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

title: Darius invades Scythia
description: Persian king Darius I campaigns against the Scythians, who retreat and avoid battle.
source: Wikipedia: Darius the Great’s European Scythian campaign

title: Yermak’s expedition to Siberia
description: Cossacks under Yermak defeat the Khanate of Sibir, opening Siberia to Russian conquest.

title: Usman dan Fodio’s jihad
description: Usman dan Fodio launches a jihad that creates the Sokoto Caliphate.

title: Nelson Mandela elected president
description: South Africa’s first elections open to all make Mandela president.

title: Cueva de las Manos
description: Hunters in Patagonia paint hundreds of hand stencils on a cave wall.

title: Arauco War: Lautaro defeats Valdivia
description: Mapuche leader Lautaro defeats and kills Spanish governor Pedro de Valdivia at Tucapel.

title: Hudson’s Bay Company founded
description: The fur-trading company is founded; Cree and other nations become its trading partners.

title: Sudan becomes independent
description: Sudan gains independence from British–Egyptian rule.

title: South Sudan secedes
description: After decades of war, South Sudan becomes independent.

title: Spain takes Jolo
description: Spanish forces capture Jolo, capital of the Sulu Sultanate.

title: First Nobel Prizes
description: The first Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm.

title: Norway leaves the union with Sweden
description: Norway peacefully ends its union with Sweden.
source: Wikipedia: Dissolution of the union between Norway and Sweden

title: Fifth Dalai Lama rules Tibet
description: With Mongol support, the Fifth Dalai Lama becomes ruler of Tibet; work on the Potala Palace begins in 1645.

title: Gateway of the Sun
description: Tiwanaku builders carve the Gateway of the Sun near Lake Titicaca.

title: Tula rises
description: Tula becomes the Toltec capital in central Mexico.

title: Bayinnaung takes Ayutthaya
