description: King Bayinnaung of Toungoo conquers Ayutthaya, part of the largest empire in Southeast Asian history.

title: Valdivia pottery
description: Villagers on the coast of Ecuador make some of the oldest pottery in the Americas.

title: Venezuela leaves Gran Colombia
description: Venezuela becomes a separate republic under José Antonio Páez.

title: Đổi Mới reforms
description: Vietnam opens its economy to markets and foreign investment.

title: Volga Bulgaria adopts Islam
description: The Abbasid envoy Ibn Fadlan visits as the Volga Bulgars adopt Islam.

title: Nok culture
description: The Nok culture of central Nigeria makes terracotta sculptures and smelts iron.

title: Cascadia earthquake
description: A huge earthquake and tsunami strike the Pacific Northwest coast, remembered in First Nations stories.

title: Western Xia founded
description: Li Yuanhao declares himself emperor of the Tangut state.

title: Banpo village
description: A Yangshao farming village with round houses and painted pottery near Xi’an.

title: Zaydi imamate founded
description: Al-Hadi ila’l-Haqq founds the Zaydi imamate at Saada; it lasts until 1962.

title: Monte Albán founded
description: The Zapotecs build their mountaintop capital in Oaxaca.

title: Spanish Civil War
description: Nationalists led by Franco defeat the Republic (1936–39); a dictatorship follows until 1975.

title: Spain becomes a democracy
description: A new constitution after Franco’s death makes Spain a parliamentary monarchy.

title: Oil found in the North Sea
description: The Ekofisk oil field is discovered, making Norway rich.

title: March on Rome
description: Mussolini’s Fascists take power in Italy.

title: Libya becomes independent
description: Libya becomes an independent kingdom under King Idris.

title: Libyan civil war
description: An uprising backed by NATO airstrikes overthrows Muammar Gaddafi.

title: Kazakhstan becomes independent
description: Kazakhstan declares independence as the Soviet Union breaks up.

title: Angola becomes independent
description: Angola wins independence from Portugal; a civil war follows until 2002.

title: Nigeria becomes independent
description: Nigeria gains independence from Britain.

title: Nigerian Civil War
description: The south-east declares independence as Biafra (1967–70); famine kills hundreds of thousands or more.

title: Tanganyika and Zanzibar unite
description: The two countries form the United Republic of Tanzania.

title: Rouran ruler takes the title khagan
description: Shelun of the Rouran becomes the first ruler known to call himself khagan.

title: The title “Dalai Lama” is created
description: Altan Khan meets Sonam Gyatso and gives him the title Dalai Lama.

title: Battle of the Kalka River
description: Mongol forces defeat an army of Cumans and Rus’ princes.
source: Wikipedia: Battle of the Kalka River

title: Megalithic burials in southern India
description: Iron Age peoples bury their dead in stone circles and urns, as at Adichanallur.

title: Irish Free State founded
description: After the War of Independence, most of Ireland becomes the Irish Free State; Northern Ireland stays in the UK.

title: National Health Service founded
description: Britain creates free health care for all, paid for by taxes.

title: Good Friday Agreement
description: A peace agreement ends three decades of conflict in Northern Ireland.

title: North Sea flood
description: A storm surge floods the Netherlands, Belgium and England, killing over 2,500 people; the Dutch then build the Delta Works.

title: Carnation Revolution
description: A nearly bloodless coup ends Portugal’s dictatorship and its colonial wars.

title: Poland regains independence
description: Poland is reborn after 123 years of partition.

title: Solidarity founded
description: Shipyard workers in Gdańsk form the first independent trade union in the Soviet bloc.

title: Ukraine becomes independent
description: Over 90% vote for independence from the Soviet Union.

title: Greek War of Independence
description: Greeks revolt against Ottoman rule; independence is recognised in 1830.

title: First modern Olympic Games
description: The modern Olympics begin in Athens.

title: Red Cross founded
description: Henry Dunant founds the International Committee of the Red Cross in Geneva.
source: Wikipedia: International Committee of the Red Cross

title: Anschluss
description: Nazi Germany annexes Austria.

title: Austrian State Treaty
description: Allied occupation ends and Austria becomes neutral.

title: Belgian Revolution
description: Belgium breaks away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.

title: Winter War
description: Finland resists a Soviet invasion (1939–40) but loses part of Karelia.

title: Iceland becomes a republic
description: Iceland ends its union with Denmark.

title: Hungarian Revolution
description: A national uprising is crushed by Soviet troops.

title: Treaty of Trianon
description: Hungary loses about two-thirds of its former territory.

title: Romanian Revolution
description: A violent uprising overthrows Nicolae Ceaușescu.

title: Union of Wallachia and Moldavia
description: The two principalities unite, forming Romania.

title: Liberation of Bulgaria
description: After the Russo-Turkish War, Bulgaria becomes autonomous.

title: Prague Spring
description: Reforms in Czechoslovakia are crushed by a Warsaw Pact invasion.

title: Velvet Revolution
description: Peaceful protests end communist rule in Czechoslovakia.

title: Czechoslovakia splits peacefully
description: Czechia and Slovakia become separate countries.

title: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes
description: South Slav lands unite in a new kingdom, later called Yugoslavia.

title: Tito–Stalin split
description: Yugoslavia breaks with the Soviet Union and goes its own way.

title: Yugoslav Wars begin
description: Slovenia and Croatia declare independence; wars follow across the region until 2001.

title: Srebrenica genocide
description: Bosnian Serb forces kill about 8,000 Bosniak men and boys; international courts ruled it genocide.

title: Dayton Agreement
description: A peace deal ends the Bosnian War.

title: Montenegro becomes independent
description: A referendum ends the union with Serbia.

title: Prespa Agreement
description: Macedonia agrees to be called North Macedonia, ending a long dispute with Greece.

title: Albanian independence
description: Albania declares independence from the Ottoman Empire at Vlorë.

title: The Baltic Way
description: About two million people join hands across Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania to call for independence.

title: Soviet annexation of the Baltic states
description: The USSR occupies and annexes Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
source: Wikipedia: Occupation of the Baltic states

title: Belovezha Accords
description: Leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus agree to dissolve the USSR.

title: Transnistria War
description: A short war leaves Transnistria outside Moldova’s control.

title: Russo-Georgian War
description: A five-day war over South Ossetia.

title: Division of Cyprus
description: After a coup backed by Greece’s junta, Turkey invades; the island has been divided since.

title: Siege of Malta
description: Axis bombing of Malta (1940–42); the island is awarded the George Cross.
source: Wikipedia: Siege of Malta (World War II)

title: Luxembourg’s independence confirmed
description: The Treaty of London recognises Luxembourg as independent.

title: Liechtenstein becomes sovereign
description: Liechtenstein becomes a sovereign state in Napoleon’s Confederation of the Rhine.

title: Andorra’s co-princes
description: An agreement between the Count of Foix and the Bishop of Urgell creates Andorra’s shared rule.

title: Malta becomes independent
description: Malta gains independence from Britain; it becomes a republic in 1974.

title: Guinea votes “no” to France
description: Guinea rejects the French Community and becomes independent at once.

title: Mali crisis
description: A Tuareg rebellion and jihadist groups seize northern Mali; French troops intervene in 2013.

title: Thomas Sankara takes power
description: Sankara launches reforms and renames Upper Volta “Burkina Faso” (1984).

title: Coup in Niger
description: The army removes the elected president; Niger turns away from France.

title: Benin’s National Conference
description: A national conference peacefully ends military-Marxist rule; free elections follow in 1991.

title: Togo’s president assassinated
description: Sylvanus Olympio is killed in Africa’s first post-independence coup.

title: Sierra Leone Civil War
description: A brutal war (1991–2002) fuelled by diamonds.

title: Liberia declares independence
description: Liberia becomes Africa’s first independent republic.

title: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf becomes president
description: Africa’s first elected woman head of state.

title: West African Ebola epidemic
description: Ebola kills over 11,000 people in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone (2014–16).

title: The Gambia becomes independent
description: The Gambia gains independence from Britain.

title: Guinea-Bissau declares independence
description: PAIGC fighters declare independence; Portugal recognises it in 1974.

title: Mauritania abolishes slavery
description: The last country to abolish slavery by law; it became a crime in 2007.

title: Lake Nyos disaster
description: A cloud of carbon dioxide from the lake suffocates about 1,700 people.

title: Bokassa crowns himself emperor
description: Jean-Bédel Bokassa holds a lavish coronation.

title: Chadian–Libyan War
description: Chad defeats Libyan forces by 1987 in the “Toyota War”.

title: Equatorial Guinea becomes independent
description: Independence from Spain; a brutal dictatorship follows.

title: Mau Mau uprising
description: An armed rebellion against British rule in Kenya (1952–60).

title: Kenya becomes independent
description: Jomo Kenyatta leads Kenya to independence.

title: Idi Amin seizes power
description: Amin’s rule (1971–79) kills an estimated 100,000–500,000 people.

title: Burundian Civil War
description: War between Hutu and Tutsi groups (1993–2005).

title: Ethiopian Revolution
description: Emperor Haile Selassie is overthrown by the Derg.

title: Ethiopian famine
description: Famine (1983–85) kills hundreds of thousands; Live Aid raises money.

title: Somalia is formed
description: British and Italian Somaliland unite as Somalia.

title: Somali Civil War
description: The government collapses; war and famine follow.

title: Djibouti becomes independent
description: Independence from France.

title: Tunisia becomes independent
description: Independence from France under Habib Bourguiba.

title: Zambia becomes independent
description: Northern Rhodesia becomes Zambia under Kenneth Kaunda.

title: Rhodesia declares independence
description: The white-minority government breaks from Britain; a war follows.

title: Zimbabwe is born
description: Majority rule and independence under Robert Mugabe.

title: Mozambique becomes independent
description: FRELIMO leads Mozambique to independence from Portugal.

title: Diamonds found in Botswana
description: The Orapa find begins Botswana’s rise.

title: Namibia becomes independent
description: Independence from South Africa.

title: Lesotho becomes independent
description: Basutoland becomes the Kingdom of Lesotho.

title: Swaziland becomes independent
description: Independence from Britain under King Sobhuza II.

title: Eritrea becomes independent
description: After a 30-year war, Eritrea votes for independence from Ethiopia.

title: Ecuador becomes independent
description: Ecuador leaves Gran Colombia under Juan José Flores.

title: Ecuadorian–Peruvian War
description: Peru defeats Ecuador; the 1942 Rio Protocol gives Peru much of the disputed Amazon.

title: Ecuador adopts the US dollar
description: After a banking crisis, Ecuador replaces the sucre with the dollar.

title: Uruguay becomes independent
description: The Treaty of Montevideo creates Uruguay as a buffer between Brazil and Argentina.

title: First FIFA World Cup
description: Uruguay hosts and wins the first football World Cup.

title: Coup in Uruguay
description: The military takes power; dictatorship lasts until 1985.

title: Central America declares independence
description: Guatemala City leaders declare independence from Spain; the federation breaks up in 1838–41.
source: Wikipedia: Act of Independence of Central America

title: Guatemalan coup
description: A CIA-backed coup overthrows President Jacobo Árbenz after his land reform.

title: Guatemalan Civil War
description: A 36-year war (1960–96); about 200,000 killed, mostly Maya, including acts judged genocide.

title: Football War
description: A four-day war between El Salvador and Honduras, sparked by migration tensions and World Cup qualifiers.

title: Hurricane Mitch
description: Floods and landslides kill about 11,000 people in Central America, most in Honduras and Nicaragua.

title: Nicaraguan Revolution
description: The Sandinistas overthrow the Somoza dictatorship; a war with US-backed Contras follows.

title: Salvadoran Civil War
description: War between the army and FMLN guerrillas (1980–92); about 75,000 killed.

title: Archbishop Óscar Romero murdered
description: Shot while saying Mass after speaking against army killings.

title: Costa Rica abolishes its army
description: After a short civil war, José Figueres abolishes the army.

title: Panama separates from Colombia
description: With US backing, Panama becomes independent and signs a canal treaty.
source: Wikipedia: Separation of Panama from Colombia

title: Panama Canal opens
description: The US-built canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

title: US invasion of Panama
description: US troops remove Manuel Noriega.
source: Wikipedia: United States invasion of Panama

title: Panama takes over the canal
description: The United States hands the canal to Panama.

title: Cuban Revolution
description: Fidel Castro’s rebels overthrow Batista; Cuba becomes a communist state.

title: Bay of Pigs invasion
description: A CIA-backed exile force fails to overthrow Castro.

title: Haiti declares independence
description: Jean-Jacques Dessalines declares Haiti the first free Black republic.

title: US occupation of Haiti
description: US Marines occupy Haiti until 1934.
source: Wikipedia: United States occupation of Haiti

title: Haiti earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake kills over 100,000 people around Port-au-Prince.

title: Dominican Republic independence
description: The east of Hispaniola breaks away from Haiti.

title: Parsley massacre
description: Dictator Trujillo’s army kills thousands of Haitians along the border.

title: Jamaica becomes independent
description: Jamaica gains independence from Britain.

title: Trinidad and Tobago becomes independent
description: Eric Williams leads the islands to independence.

title: Guyana becomes independent
description: British Guiana becomes Guyana.

title: Barbados becomes a republic
description: Barbados replaces the British monarch with an elected president.

title: The Bahamas becomes independent
description: Independence from Britain under Lynden Pindling.

title: Suriname becomes independent
description: Independence from the Netherlands; many people move to the Netherlands.

title: Belize becomes independent
description: British Honduras becomes Belize; British troops stay to deter Guatemala.

title: US invasion of Grenada
description: After Maurice Bishop is killed, US-led forces invade.
source: Wikipedia: United States invasion of Grenada

title: Hurricane Maria hits Dominica
description: A Category 5 hurricane damages almost every building on Dominica.

title: Saint Lucia becomes independent
description: Independence from Britain.

title: La Soufrière erupts
description: The volcano erupts; about 20,000 people are evacuated.

title: Antigua and Barbuda becomes independent
description: Independence from Britain under Vere Bird.

title: Saint Kitts and Nevis becomes independent
description: The last British colony in the Caribbean to become a full state.

title: Iraq becomes independent
description: The British mandate ends and Iraq joins the League of Nations.

title: Iran–Iraq War
description: Iraq invades Iran; eight years of trench warfare and chemical attacks kill hundreds of thousands.

title: Gulf War
description: Iraq invades Kuwait; a US-led coalition drives it out in early 1991.

title: Islamic State seizes Mosul
description: The ISIS group declares a “caliphate” across Iraq and Syria; it is defeated by 2019.

title: Fall of the Assad government
description: Rebels take Damascus and Bashar al-Assad flees to Russia.
source: Wikipedia: Fall of the Assad regime

title: Lebanon becomes independent
description: The National Pact shares power among religious communities.

title: Lebanese Civil War
description: A war among militias and foreign forces (1975–90) kills about 150,000.

title: Beirut port explosion
description: Stored ammonium nitrate explodes, killing over 200 people.

title: Jordan becomes independent
description: Transjordan becomes the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.

title: Black September
description: Jordan’s army expels Palestinian armed groups from the country.

title: Yom Kippur War
description: Egypt and Syria attack Israel; the war leads to the oil embargo and later peace talks.

title: Egypt–Israel peace treaty
description: After the Camp David Accords, Egypt becomes the first Arab state to recognise Israel.

title: United Arab Emirates founded
description: Six Trucial States unite; Ras al-Khaimah joins in 1972.

title: World Cup in Qatar
description: The first football World Cup held in the Arab world.

title: Kuwait becomes independent
description: The British protectorate ends; British troops deter an Iraqi claim.

title: Qaboos becomes Sultan of Oman
description: Qaboos replaces his father and opens and modernises the country.

title: Oman and Zanzibar split
description: After Said bin Sultan dies, his empire divides between two sons.

title: North Yemen revolution
description: Army officers overthrow the Zaydi imam; a civil war follows until 1970.

title: Yemen unites
description: North and South Yemen join as one republic.

title: Yemeni Civil War
description: Houthi rebels take Sana’a; a Saudi-led coalition intervenes in 2015.

title: Spitak earthquake
description: An earthquake in Soviet Armenia kills about 25,000 people.

title: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
description: Armenians and Azerbaijanis fight over Karabakh (1988–94); hundreds of thousands are displaced.

title: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
description: Azerbaijan retakes much of the region; in 2023 the remaining Armenian population leaves.

title: The Aral Sea begins to shrink
description: Soviet cotton irrigation diverts its rivers; the sea loses most of its water.

title: Tajik Civil War
description: War between the government and an Islamist–democratic opposition (1992–97).

title: Tulip Revolution
description: Protests overthrow Kyrgyz president Askar Akayev.

title: Turkmenistan declares neutrality
description: The UN recognises its permanent neutrality.

title: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
description: A war over Kashmir ends in a ceasefire.

title: Bangladesh Liberation War
description: East Pakistan breaks away with Indian help; the Pakistani army kills hundreds of thousands.

title: Pakistan tests nuclear weapons
description: Tests in the Chagai Hills follow India’s tests.

title: Pakistan floods
description: Record monsoon rains flood a third of the country.

title: Bengali Language Movement
description: Students in Dhaka are killed protesting for Bengali as a state language; 21 February is now International Mother Language Day.

title: Bhola cyclone
description: One of the deadliest cyclones ever; up to 500,000 die in East Pakistan.

title: Rana Plaza collapse
description: A garment factory building collapses near Dhaka, killing 1,134 workers.

title: Ceylon becomes independent
description: Ceylon gains independence from Britain; it becomes Sri Lanka in 1972.

title: Sri Lankan Civil War
description: The Tamil Tigers fight for a separate state (1983–2009); the war ends with heavy civilian deaths.

title: Gorkha conquest of Kathmandu
description: Prithvi Narayan Shah takes the Kathmandu valley and unifies Nepal.

title: Anglo-Nepalese War
description: Nepal loses land to the British East India Company (1814–16); Gurkha recruitment begins.

title: First ascent of Everest
description: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reach the summit.

title: Nepal becomes a republic
description: After a Maoist civil war, the 240-year-old monarchy is abolished.

title: Nepal earthquake
description: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake kills about 9,000 people.

title: Zhabdrung arrives in Bhutan
description: Ngawang Namgyal flees Tibet and unifies Bhutan under a Buddhist state.

title: Wangchuck monarchy founded
description: Ugyen Wangchuck is chosen as the first hereditary king.

title: Burma becomes independent
description: Burma leaves the British Empire, months after Aung San is assassinated.

title: 8888 Uprising
description: Mass protests against military rule are crushed; Aung San Suu Kyi emerges as leader.

title: Rohingya crisis
description: An army crackdown drives over 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh.

title: Myanmar coup
description: The army seizes power; resistance grows into a civil war.

title: Cambodia becomes independent
description: King Norodom Sihanouk wins independence from France.

title: Vietnam ends Khmer Rouge rule
description: Vietnamese troops take Phnom Penh in January 1979.

title: Laos becomes independent
description: France recognises full independence.

title: US bombing of Laos
description: The US drops over 2 million tonnes of bombs on Laos (1964–73).

title: Brunei becomes fully independent
description: The British protectorate ends.

title: Two Korean states founded
description: The Republic of Korea (south) and the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (north) are declared.

title: Gwangju Uprising
description: Troops kill hundreds of pro-democracy protesters.

title: Seoul Olympics
description: South Korea hosts the Olympics after its move to democracy.

title: North Korean famine
description: Famine (1994–98) kills hundreds of thousands.

title: North Korea’s first nuclear test
description: North Korea tests a nuclear weapon.

title: Women win the vote in New Zealand
description: New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country to give women the vote.
source: Wikipedia: Women’s suffrage in New Zealand

title: New Zealand Wars
description: Wars between the colonial government and Māori iwi over land (1845–72).

title: Christchurch earthquake
description: An earthquake kills 185 people and destroys much of the city centre.

title: Kokoda Track campaign
description: Australian troops, helped by Papuan carriers, stop the Japanese advance on Port Moresby.

title: Papua New Guinea becomes independent
description: Independence from Australia under Michael Somare.

title: Bougainville conflict
description: A war over a copper mine and independence (1988–98).

title: Fiji ceded to Britain
description: Chief Cakobau cedes Fiji to Queen Victoria.

title: Fiji coups
description: Sitiveni Rabuka seizes power twice in 1987.

title: Samoa becomes independent
description: The first Pacific island nation to win independence.

title: Black Saturday in Samoa
description: New Zealand police fire on a peaceful Mau protest, killing the leader Tupua Tamasese Lealofi III.

title: Tonga united
description: George Tupou I unites Tonga; its 1875 constitution is still in force.

title: Hunga Tonga eruption
description: One of the largest volcanic explosions ever recorded; a tsunami hits Tonga.
source: Wikipedia: 2022 Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai eruption and tsunami

title: Battle of Morgarten
description: Swiss peasants ambush and defeat a Habsburg army.

title: Zwingli’s Reformation in Zürich
description: Zürich adopts the Reformation; the Swiss cantons split by religion.

title: French invasion of Switzerland
description: France conquers the Confederacy and sets up the Helvetic Republic.

title: Reign of Terror
description: The revolutionary government executes about 17,000 people (1793–94).

title: Napoleon crowns himself emperor
description: Napoleon becomes Emperor of the French at Notre-Dame.

title: Battles of Jena and Auerstedt
description: Napoleon crushes the Prussian army.

title: Kingdom of Prussia proclaimed
description: Elector Frederick III crowns himself King Frederick I in Königsberg.

title: Seven Years’ War
description: Prussia survives a war against Austria, France and Russia (1756–63).

title: German customs union
description: Most German states join a Prussian-led customs union.

title: German Confederation founded
description: The Congress of Vienna joins 39 German states in a loose league.

title: Peace of Lodi
description: Milan, Venice, Florence, Naples and the Papacy agree a balance of power.

title: Italian Wars begin
description: France invades Italy; Spain and France fight over it until 1559.

title: German hyperinflation
description: Prices double every few days; savings are wiped out.
source: Wikipedia: Hyperinflation in the Weimar Republic

title: East German uprising
description: Workers’ protests are crushed by Soviet tanks.

title: Britain takes Hong Kong Island
description: During the First Opium War Britain occupies the island; China cedes it in 1842 (Treaty of Nanking).

title: New Territories leased
description: China leases the New Territories to Britain for 99 years.
source: Wikipedia: Convention for the Extension of Hong Kong Territory

title: Japan occupies Hong Kong
description: Japan captures Hong Kong on Christmas Day 1941 and holds it until 1945.
source: Wikipedia: Japanese occupation of Hong Kong

title: Hong Kong protests
description: Mass protests against an extradition bill; a National Security Law follows in 2020.

title: Puerto Rico becomes a Commonwealth
description: A new constitution makes Puerto Rico a self-governing US territory.

title: Hurricane Maria hits Puerto Rico
description: The island loses power for months; about 3,000 people die.

title: Danish mission to Greenland
description: Hans Egede founds a mission and trading post, beginning Danish colonial rule.

title: Greenland home rule
description: Greenland gets its own parliament; self-government follows in 2009.

title: Oil found in Bahrain
description: The first oil discovery on the Arab side of the Gulf.

title: Bahrain becomes independent
description: The British protectorate ends.

title: Bahraini uprising
description: Pro-democracy protests are put down with help from Saudi troops.

title: Maldives becomes independent
description: The British protectorate ends; the sultanate becomes a republic in 1968.

title: Underwater cabinet meeting
description: Ministers meet in scuba gear to warn about rising seas.

title: Mauritius becomes independent
description: Independence from Britain under Seewoosagur Ramgoolam.

title: Seychelles becomes independent
description: Independence from Britain; a coup follows in 1977.

title: Comoros declares independence
description: Three islands leave France; Mayotte votes to stay French.

title: Cabo Verde becomes independent
description: Independence from Portugal after the Carnation Revolution.

title: São Tomé and Príncipe becomes independent
description: Independence from Portugal.

title: East Timor votes for independence
description: Nearly 80% vote to leave Indonesia; militias destroy much of the country before UN troops arrive.

title: Timor-Leste becomes independent
description: The first new sovereign state of the 21st century.

title: South Sudanese Civil War
description: Fighting between forces loyal to Salva Kiir and Riek Machar (2013–18) kills about 400,000.

title: Portuguese settle in Macau
description: Ming officials let Portuguese traders settle on the peninsula.

title: Macau returns to China
description: Portugal hands Macau to China as a Special Administrative Region.
source: Wikipedia: Transfer of sovereignty over Macau

title: Guadalcanal campaign
description: US and Allied forces defeat Japan in a six-month battle (1942–43).

title: Solomon Islands becomes independent
description: Independence from Britain.

title: Vanuatu becomes independent
description: The New Hebrides condominium ends.

title: Nuclear tests at Bikini Atoll
description: The US begins nuclear tests; islanders are moved and never fully return.
source: Wikipedia: Nuclear testing at Bikini Atoll

title: Castle Bravo test
description: The largest US nuclear test spreads fallout over inhabited atolls.

title: Compact of Free Association
description: The Marshall Islands and Micronesia become self-governing in free association with the US.

title: Palau becomes independent
description: The last UN Trust Territory ends.

title: Battle of Peleliu
description: A costly US assault on a Japanese-held island in Palau.

title: Nauru becomes independent
description: The smallest republic takes over its phosphate industry.

title: Battle of Tarawa
description: US Marines capture the atoll in three days of heavy fighting.

title: Kiribati becomes independent
description: The Gilbert Islands leave British rule.

title: Tuvalu becomes independent
description: The Ellice Islands become Tuvalu.

title: Grimaldis seize Monaco
description: François Grimaldi, disguised as a monk, takes the fortress.

title: Monte Carlo casino opens
description: Gambling makes Monaco rich.

title: San Marino’s statutes
description: Written laws that still form part of its constitution.

title: Lateran Treaty
description: Italy recognises Vatican City as an independent state.

title: Second Vatican Council
description: Major reforms of the Catholic Church (1962–65), including Mass in local languages.

title: Roman currency collapses
description: During the Crisis of the Third Century, emperors cut the silver in the denarius to pay soldiers; prices soar and trade falls back on barter. Diocletian’s price edict (301) fails to stop it.
source: Wikipedia: Crisis of the Third Century

title: Yuan paper money loses its value
description: The Mongol Yuan government prints ever more paper money to pay its debts; inflation helps bring on the revolts that end the dynasty in 1368.

title: Spain’s first state bankruptcy
description: Despite American silver, Philip II stops paying his bankers; Spain defaults again in 1560, 1575, 1596 and later.

title: First publicly traded company
description: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) sells shares to the public; Amsterdam becomes the first modern stock market.

title: Tulip mania
description: Prices for rare tulip bulbs in the Dutch Republic rise to the cost of a house, then crash in February 1637.

title: Ming China’s silver crisis
description: Less silver arrives from Japan and the Americas just as harvests fail; taxes paid in silver become crushing, feeding the revolts that topple the Ming in 1644.

title: South Sea Bubble
description: Shares of the South Sea Company soar and crash, ruining many investors in Britain.

title: Mississippi Bubble
description: John Law’s paper-money and Louisiana company scheme collapses in France, making the French wary of banks and paper money for generations.

title: French crown runs out of money
description: War debts leave the crown unable to borrow; Louis XVI calls the Estates-General, which leads to the Revolution in 1789.
source: Wikipedia: Causes of the French Revolution

title: Panic of 1873
description: The Vienna stock market crashes in May and New York in September, starting the Long Depression in Europe and North America.

title: Bretton Woods conference
description: Allied countries agree a post-war money system tied to the US dollar and create the IMF and World Bank.

title: End of the gold standard
description: The US stops exchanging dollars for gold; the world moves to floating currencies.

title: Latin American debt crisis
description: Mexico cannot pay its foreign debts; a “lost decade” of slow growth follows across Latin America.

title: Japan’s bubble bursts
description: Japanese share and land prices collapse, beginning the “lost decades” of slow growth.

title: Russia’s economic collapse
description: Prices are freed after the Soviet Union ends; inflation passes 2,000% and the economy shrinks sharply; Russia defaults in 1998.

title: Argentine economic crisis
description: Bank accounts are frozen, riots topple the government and Argentina makes the largest debt default of its time.

title: Zimbabwe’s hyperinflation
description: Prices double every day at the peak; a 100-trillion-dollar note is printed and the currency is abandoned in 2009.

title: Greek and eurozone debt crisis
description: Greece cannot pay its debts; bailouts come with deep cuts, and the crisis spreads to Ireland, Portugal, Spain and Cyprus.

title: COVID-19 recession
description: Lockdowns cause the sharpest fall in world output since the Great Depression; governments spend on a huge scale.

title: Sri Lanka defaults
description: Sri Lanka runs out of foreign currency for fuel and food; protests force the president to flee.

title: French take Ouagadougou
description: French troops occupy the Mossi capital; Mogho Naba Wobgo flees.

title: Dahomey conquers Ouidah
description: King Agaja takes the slave-trading port of Ouidah.

title: Second Franco-Dahomean War
description: France defeats King Béhanzin and his women soldiers.

title: Uganda Martyrs
description: Kabaka Mwanga II has Christian converts at his court killed.

title: Buganda Agreement
description: Buganda accepts British rule in return for land and self-government.

title: Lozi treaty with Britain
description: Litunga Lewanika signs a concession with the British South Africa Company.

title: First Matabele War
description: British South Africa Company forces with machine guns defeat Lobengula.

title: Rozvi drive out the Portuguese
description: Changamire Dombo defeats the Portuguese on the Zimbabwe plateau.

title: Umar Tall’s jihad begins
description: El Hadj Umar Tall starts the wars that create the Toucouleur Empire.

title: Futa Jallon jihad
description: Muslim Fula leaders found an Islamic state in the Guinea highlands.

title: Samori Touré captured
description: After 16 years of war, the French capture Samori; he dies in exile in 1900.

title: Samori destroys Kong
description: Samori’s army burns the trading city of Kong.

title: Ségou kingdom founded
description: Biton Coulibaly builds a Bambara kingdom on the Niger.

title: France takes Abéché
description: French forces capture the Wadai capital.

title: Egypt conquers Sennar
description: Muhammad Ali’s army ends the Funj Sultanate.

title: Anglo-Zanzibar War
description: British warships force out a new sultan in about 40 minutes, the shortest war on record.

title: Zanzibar Revolution
description: African revolutionaries overthrow the sultan; thousands of Arabs and South Asians are killed.

title: Gold found on the Witwatersrand
description: The world’s biggest gold field is found; Johannesburg is founded.

title: Second Boer War
description: Britain defeats the Boer republics (1899–1902); about 26,000 Boer women and children and at least 14,000 Black Africans die in British camps.

title: Asante defeats Denkyira
description: The new Asante kingdom overthrows its Akan overlord.

title: Battle of Shimbra Kure
description: Ahmad Gragn defeats the Ethiopian army and overruns much of the empire (1529–43).

title: Arab Revolt
description: Sharif Hussein of Mecca rises against the Ottomans with British support.

title: Ibn Saud takes the Hejaz
description: Saudi forces take Mecca (1924) and Jeddah (1925).

title: Battle of Mulayda
description: The Rashidis of Ha’il defeat the Saudis and take Riyadh.

title: Ibn Saud captures Ha’il
description: The Rashidi emirate ends.

title: English Reformation
description: Henry VIII breaks with Rome and makes himself head of the Church of England.

title: Spanish Armada defeated
description: England beats off Philip II’s invasion fleet.

title: English Civil War
description: Parliament defeats Charles I, who is executed in 1649; England becomes a republic until 1660.

title: Glorious Revolution
description: James II is replaced by William and Mary; the Bill of Rights (1689) limits the crown.

title: Battle of Bannockburn
description: Robert the Bruce defeats Edward II and secures Scotland’s independence.

title: Scottish Reformation
description: Scotland becomes Protestant under John Knox’s influence.

title: Union of the Crowns
description: James VI of Scotland also becomes king of England and Ireland.

title: Plantation of Ulster
description: English and Scottish Protestants are settled on land taken from Irish lords.

title: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland
description: Cromwell’s army takes Drogheda and Wexford; much Catholic land is confiscated.

title: Irish Rebellion of 1798
description: The United Irishmen rise with French help; the revolt leads to the Act of Union.

title: Siam sacks Longvek
description: The Cambodian capital falls to Ayutthaya.

title: Cambodia becomes a French protectorate
description: King Norodom accepts French protection against Siam and Vietnam.

title: Lan Xang splits
description: The Lao kingdom divides into Luang Prabang and Vientiane (Champasak follows in 1713).

title: Lao rebellion against Siam
description: King Anouvong of Vientiane rises against Siam; Vientiane is destroyed in 1828.

title: Shan states take Ava
description: A Shan confederation captures Ava, ruling Upper Burma until 1555.

title: Mrauk U founded
description: King Min Saw Mon returns from exile in Bengal and founds a new capital.

title: Burma conquers Arakan
description: Konbaung armies take Mrauk U and carry the Mahamuni Buddha to Amarapura.

title: Karim Khan rebuilds Shiraz
description: The Zand ruler makes Shiraz his capital with a new bazaar, mosque and citadel.

title: Australian Frontier Wars
description: Aboriginal nations resist British settlement, starting with Pemulwuy near Sydney (1790); fighting and massacres continue on the frontier into the 1930s.
